verdicts.summary: The new NOT EXISTS clause sits only in the fresh-arm OR branch. It is read-only and keyed on the direct parent's settledOverride. Already-armed children still resume through the first branch.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four cases. (1) A child already armed before the parent settled. The first OR branch (3958-3967) has no parent check, so it still resumes. (2) A non-subagent child, or a child with a null or malformed parentThreadId. The EXISTS subquery finds no parent row, so NOT EXISTS is true and the thread is armed as before. (3) The parent is later unsettled. The settledOverride check then fails, so the child becomes a candidate again. (4) A grandparent is settled but the direct parent is not. The clause only checks the direct parent, so the child is armed. I judged that acceptable because the parent is live. The same relationshipToParent='subagent' lineage JSON path is used elsewhere in this file, so the key name is right.
